claims.statement: Tom Allen fought Joe Goss near Walton, Kentucky, on September 7, 1876, and Goss was awarded the fight on a foul in the twenty-first round.
claims.excerpt: Goss falls and is struck by Allen while cn his knees. A foul claimed and allowed. Fight decided in favor of Goss

claims.statement: Eph Holland stopped the fight after seven rounds had been fought.
claims.excerpt: and accordingly stopped the fight, after seven rounds had been fought.

claims.statement: After the militia dispersed the crowd, a second ring was formed in Boone County and the fighting went on there.
claims.excerpt: After being dispersed by the militia a second ring was formed a short distance below Walton, in Boone County.

claims.statement: Tom Allen came to the grounds with Kelley and Chambers as his seconds.
claims.excerpt: Allen, with Kelley and Chambers, his seconds,

claims.statement: Eph Holland was induced to referee the fight after several prominent pugilists declined the position.
claims.excerpt: After several prominent pugilists had declined the position of referee

claims.statement: Tom Allen was arrested at Newport when two trains from the fight were stopped by the authorities.
claims.excerpt: were siopped by the authorities, and Tom Allen arrested.

fights.excerpt: Goss falls and is struck by Allen while cn his knees. A foul claimed and allowed. Fight decided in favor of Goss
fights.notes: Stopped by the militia after seven rounds, resumed in a second ring in Boone County; Goss awarded the fight on a foul in the 21st round.

notes: Dispatch from the grounds near Walton, Kentucky. Hint about Tom Kelly spelled as Kelley in the text.
